Seal the law among my disciples” (web:Isa.8.16), and the prophet’s own first-person response follows without a fresh frame marker, closing on “Behold, I and the children whom Yahweh has given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from Yahweh of Armies, who dwells in Mount Zion.” (web:Isa.8.18); the next verse’s conditional “When they tell you” clause (web:Isa.8.19) opens a new topic. boundary_rationale: This unit is bounded by a dramatic question-and-answer frame: the prophetic voice opens with a verse-initial interrogative, מִי זֶ֣ה בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), “Who is this who comes from Edom” (web:Isa.63.1); the clause that follows opens instead on a bare demonstrative, זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), rendered as a second question, “Who is this who is glorious in his clothing,” only in the English witness. The challenged figure answers in the first person, closing that reply with "אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ" (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier) ('I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save'). The same first-person divine-warrior voice continues in unbroken speech through the vengeance-and-treading report, closing the unit at “I poured their lifeblood out on the earth.” (web:Isa.63.6). The unit ends there because 63:7 pivots to a different speaker and a different speech-act: a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report, with no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame.
